newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots mixed.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots mixed.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly down on Friday mainly due to rumours that the Shanghai stock exchange would cancel the three-day and seven-day contracts, traders said.
But an exchange spokesman told Reuters the bourse was not considering the cancellation.
"I can't confirm the rumours. We are not considering (a cancellation). We have not considered (such a cancellation)," he said.
The annual rate for the most active seven-day contract fell to 10.52 to 12.03 percent on Thursday.
Total turnover of the six-contract market fell to 7.1 million lots from 10.7 million.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.

Traders said some institutions lent large amounts of money on the market on Friday after borrowing heavily on Thursday for bidding in a domestic A share issue on the Shenzhen bourse on Friday. This was another reason for the day's falls.
"The rumours are the key factor depressing the repo rates today," said one trader. "But if the rumours are denied, the rates will quickly recover early next week."
Rates will be supported by a number of new A share issues scheduled for next week in Shanghai and Shenzhen, traders said.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mixed on Friday after falling for four days in a row due to a powerful technical correction, traders said.
The most active 10-year bond that matures in June 2006, a market barometer, rose to 117.23 yuan from 117.20, indicating the market is walking out of the correction, they said.
Combined volume of the nine-contract market rose to 917,668 lots from 713,531 lots.
